extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning arithmetic of compound interest (readers of a historical Italian mathematical treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and worked examples for computing interest (merito) and total amount (capitale + merito) over fractional and multiple periods, including methods for compounding, proportional scaling, unit-conversion across historic currency denominations, and shortcuts (cross-multiplication, factor reuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest proportional to time (merito proporzionale al tempo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest (merito) accrues in proportion to the time elapsed; to find the merito for a fractional period, scale the prescribed rate proportionally to months, days, or other subperiods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly demonstrates computing interest for e.g. a number of months by taking the annual merito and multiplying by the fraction of the year (months/12). Examples and numeric illustrations show converting yearly rates to per‑month amounts and summing them for arbitrary dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish payments at term vs periodic payments (termine vs pagamento periodico)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat sums due ‘a termine’ (paid at the end of the term) differently from payments made periodically: whether interest is taken out each term or left to accumulate affects subsequent computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author contrasts cases where merito is paid only at the final term versus where it is paid or capitalised periodically; guidance shows how to adjust the calculation (either accumulate merito into capital for compounding or keep it separate if paid out).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound interest by reinvesting interest (merito addizionato al capitale)
rubrics_metrics.description: When interest is left with the capital (reinvested), it becomes part of the capital and earns interest in subsequent periods (compound interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated by iterative examples: after each period add the merito to capitale and compute next period’s merito on the new total. The text uses repeated multiplication (geometric progression) to show growth over many periods and gives numeric sequences showing doubling/tripling over years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute amount after n periods by repeated multiplication (ripetuta moltiplicazione / potenza)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain the amount after multiple identical periods, multiply the capital by the period factor repeatedly (i.e., apply (1+rate_per_period)^n via repeated multiplication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript gives examples of multiplying the capital by the same factor for each year (or month) and shows shortcuts for doing many repeated multiplications (e.g., breaking the exponentiation into smaller factor multiplications and reusing precomputed factors). It also shows how to find the total after long sequences of years by decomposing into manageable products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert between interest and equivalent capital (passaggio tra merito e capitale)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are systematic proportional relations to express a merito amount as equivalent capital for a given period, and conversely to express capital as the merito it will produce over a period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to compute what capital would produce a given merito in a given time, or how much merito corresponds to a given capital over specified months/years, using direct proportionality and the same multiplication/division techniques used elsewhere in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross‑multiplication and multi‑unit currency arithmetic (multiplica in croci / cambio unità)
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with historical multi-unit currency (fiorini, soldi, denari), use cross‑multiplication and the described line/margin methods to combine, convert and multiply mixed units correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author prescribes arranging units in columns and 'multiplica in croci' (cross-multiply) following the currency's subunit relationships. Several worked numeric examples illustrate converting between fiorini-soldi-denari, multiplying these mixed amounts by rates, and reducing results back to standard units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale by fractional parts and handle fractional periods (parti aliquote e frazioni di periodo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute interest for non-integer numbers of periods (e.g., 7 months, 20 days) by taking the appropriate fractional part of the period’s merito and applying proportional arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript shows dividing the annual merito into monthly (or other subperiod) shares and combining fractional pieces; guidance includes examples converting e.g. merito for 7 months as (7/12) of the annual merito and handling resulting fractional coin units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine time to reach a given multiple of capital (tempo per raggiungere multipli)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find how many periods (years/months) are required for capital to grow to a specified multiple by iteratively multiplying by the period factor until the target is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods illustrated: repeated multiplication and tracking when the accumulated amount equals or exceeds the target multiple; the text gives worked examples demonstrating how to count years needed and how to decompose the exponentiation when many periods are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle payments or receipts at different dates by pro‑rata merito and aggregation (pagamenti a tempi diversi)
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple credits/debits occur at different dates, compute the merito for each to a common date (pro rata) and aggregate to get totals; adjust capital shares and merito accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author provides examples where different sums are due at different months/years and demonstrates computing merito separately to a reckoning date, then summing or reallocating amounts. Advice includes reducing all to the same time basis before comparing or combining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precomputed factors and decomposition for efficiency (tavole/fattori precomputati e scomposizione)
rubrics_metrics.description: For efficiency in repeated compounding, precompute commonly used period factors or decompose large exponents into products of known factors to avoid excessive manual multiplications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text recommends preparing factors for standard multipliers (e.g., yearly factor for a given rate) and reusing them; also demonstrates decomposing a long sequence (many years) into smaller factor multiplications (e.g., square and then multiply) to shorten computation by hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat amounts as geometric progressions and use their summation/proportional properties (progressione geometrica implicita)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the sequence of capital amounts across equal periods as a geometric progression (ratio = 1 + rate_per_period); use geometric reasoning for comparing years, summing gains, or decomposing parts between merito and capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript frames iterative capital growth as repeated application of a ratio, uses proportional parts of successive terms to reason about returns, and derives numeric relationships by manipulating the geometric sequence (examples show extracting parts of capital/growth corresponding to earlier years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize and reduce mixed results to standard coin units and simplified fractions (riduzione e normalizzazione)
rubrics_metrics.description: After multiplication and proportional operations, reduce results to the standard currency units and simplify fractional coin parts so results are expressed in canonical denominations (fiorini, soldi, denari) or lowest fractional terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous worked examples perform reduction (carryover of soldi to fiorini, denari to soldi) and simplify fractional remainders; the procedure is illustrated step‑by‑step to ensure the final amount is in proper units and comparable across examples.
